concepts.title: Stoichiometry of Hydrocarbon Combustion
concepts.definition: Complete burning of any open-chain or cyclic hydrocarbon in excess oxygen releases carbon dioxide, water, and thermal energy according to fixed stoichiometric ratios.
concepts.key_idea: Every mole of carbon produces one mole of CO2 while four hydrogens demand one mole of O2 to form two moles of H2O.
question_patterns: calculate moles of oxygen needed to completely burn a hydrocarbon
find the volume of oxygen required for combustion of alkane
how much oxygen is consumed during complete burning of hydrocarbon
what is the stoichiometric coefficient of dioxygen in hydrocarbon combustion

solution_steps.action: identify carbon and hydrogen atom counts
solution_steps.explain: from molecular formula CxHy, extract x as carbon_count and y as hydrogen_count

solution_steps.action: calculate oxygen requirement per mole of fuel
solution_steps.explain: each carbon requires one O2 and every four hydrogens require one O2

concepts.title: Counting Sigma and Pi Bonds in Hydrocarbons
concepts.definition: Counting total single covalent bonds (sigma) and multiple electron overlaps (pi) across open-chain and branched unsaturated hydrocarbons.
concepts.formula: sigma_bonds = total_atoms - 1 + rings, pi_bonds = double_bonds + 2 x triple_bonds
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, Every single bond is a sigma bond, every double bond contributes one sigma and one pi, and each triple bond has one sigma and two pi bonds.
question_patterns: calculate number of sigma and pi bonds in the given hydrocarbon
find the count of sigma and pi bonds in an unsaturated compound
how many sigma bonds and pi bonds are present in molecule
what is the total number of sigma and pi bonds

solution_steps.action: sum all single bonds and one component of each multiple bond
solution_steps.explain: in an acyclic hydrocarbon, total sigma bonds equal total atoms minus one

solution_steps.action: compute total pi bonds from multiple bond multiplicity
solution_steps.explain: each double bond contributes one pi bond and each triple bond contributes two pi bonds

concepts.title: Hückel Rule of Aromaticity
concepts.definition: A cyclic, planar, fully conjugated ring system possesses aromatic stability if its delocalized pi-electron cloud equals (4n + 2), where n is a non-negative integer.
concepts.key_idea: An odd number of electron pairs ((4n+2) electrons) delocalized over a planar ring confers aromatic character.
question_patterns: calculate the value of n in Huckel rule for aromatic ring
find if the given pi electron count satisfies Huckel rule
how many pi electrons are required for Huckel aromaticity
determine the aromaticity integer n for conjugated ring

solution_steps.action: subtract 2 from total delocalized pi electrons
solution_steps.explain: the offset of 2 accounts for the lowest closed electron shell

solution_steps.action: divide the difference by four to determine Hückel index
solution_steps.explain: if n is a whole integer (0, 1, 2, ...), the electron count obeys the (4n+2) rule

concepts.title: Chain and Position Isomerism of Alkanes and Alkenes
concepts.definition: Hydrocarbons with identical molecular formulas can differ either by the skeleton connectivity of carbon chains or by the location of functional groups and multiple bonds.
concepts.key_idea: Skeletal branching creates chain isomers, while varying the location of the unsaturation site generates position isomers.
question_patterns: write structures and IUPAC names of chain isomers
identify position and chain isomers for given formula
how many structural isomers can be formed for hydrocarbon
distinguish between chain and position isomers

solution_steps.action: draw all continuous and branched carbon skeletons
solution_steps.explain: generate distinct parent chain lengths starting from the longest continuous chain down to shorter branched variants.

solution_steps.action: place functional groups or unsaturation at non-equivalent positions
solution_steps.explain: shift multiple bonds or substituents across symmetry-inequivalent carbons and assign systematic IUPAC names.

concepts.title: Conformations of Ethane and Torsional Strain
concepts.definition: Infinite spatial arrangements produced by free rotation around the carbon-carbon single bond in ethane, bounded by the low-energy staggered and high-energy eclipsed conformations.
concepts.key_idea: Staggered conformation minimizes repulsive overlap between C-H electron clouds, making it more stable than the eclipsed form.
question_patterns: draw Sawhorse and Newman projections for ethane conformers
compare the relative stability of staggered and eclipsed ethane
what is torsional strain in conformational analysis
explain why staggered conformation of ethane is preferred

solution_steps.action: represent ethane using Sawhorse or Newman projections
solution_steps.explain: depict front and rear carbon C-H bonds separated by a dihedral angle of 60 degrees for staggered and 0 degrees for eclipsed.

solution_steps.action: evaluate torsional repulsion between adjacent bond electron clouds
solution_steps.explain: staggered form has maximal separation and least torsional strain, whereas eclipsed form has highest electron cloud repulsion.

concepts.title: Geometrical Isomerism in Alkenes
concepts.definition: Diastereomeric isomerism arising from restricted rotation about the carbon-carbon double bond when each doubly bonded carbon bears two distinct substituents.
concepts.formula: cis: similar groups on same side; trans: similar groups on opposite sides
concepts.key_idea: Restricted pi-bond rotation fixes spatial orientation, producing polar cis isomers and generally more symmetric, higher melting trans isomers.
question_patterns: which of the following alkenes will show cis-trans isomerism

solution_steps.action: check the two substituents on each sp2 carbon atom
solution_steps.explain: confirm that neither doubly bonded carbon is attached to two identical groups (requires abC=Cab or abC=Ccd).

solution_steps.action: assign cis or trans designation and compare dipole moments
solution_steps.explain: identify if identical groups lie on the same side (cis) or opposite sides (trans), and evaluate vector cancellation of bond dipole moments.

concepts.title: Markovnikov and Anti-Markovnikov Electrophilic Addition
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, Polar electrophilic addition of hydrogen halides to unsymmetrical alkenes directs the halide to the more substituted carbon, while organic peroxides reverse the regioselectivity for HBr via a free-radical intermediate.
concepts.formula: Markovnikov: electrophile H+ adds to carbon with more H; Peroxide: Br radical adds to carbon with more H
concepts.key_idea: Markovnikov addition proceeds via the more stable carbocation intermediate, while peroxide-catalyzed addition of HBr proceeds via the more stable alkyl free radical.
question_patterns: predict the major product of addition of HBr to propene
explain the peroxide effect on addition of HBr to unsymmetrical alkenes
why is peroxide effect observed with HBr but not with HCl or HI
write the mechanism for Markovnikov addition of hydrogen halide

solution_steps.action: determine whether reaction is ionic or radical-mediated
solution_steps.explain: ionic conditions follow Markovnikov's rule via the more substituted stable carbocation; presence of peroxides with HBr triggers free-radical chain addition.

solution_steps.action: attach the electrophile and nucleophile to the respective alkene carbons
solution_steps.explain: for Markovnikov, place Br at the less-hydrogenated carbon; for Kharasch peroxide conditions with HBr, place Br at the terminal, more-hydrogenated carbon.

concepts.title: Alkene Ozonolysis and Double Bond Cleavage
concepts.definition: In brief, Oxidative cleavage of an alkene's carbon-carbon double bond with ozone followed by zinc-water reductive workup, yielding aldehydes and ketones corresponding to the substitution pattern.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, Cleaving the C=C both bond and capping both resulting fragments with carbonyl oxygens reveals the original's location and branching double bond.
question_patterns: deduce the structural formula of alkene from ozonolysis products
write IUPAC names of products formed by ozonolysis of alkene
identify the alkene which gives two moles of ethanal on ozonolysis
what carbonyl compounds are obtained from reductive ozonolysis

solution_steps.action: break the C=C double bond into two carbonyl precursors
solution_steps.explain: form an intermediate molozonide/ozonide across the double bond.

solution_steps.action: replace the split double bond fragments with carbonyl oxygen atoms
solution_steps.explain: reductive cleavage with Zn and H2O converts =CH- groups to aldehydes and =C(R)- groups to ketones without further oxidation to carboxylic acids.

concepts.title: Acidity of Terminal Alkynes
concepts.definition: Hydrogen atoms attached directly to sp-hybridized carbons in terminal alkynes exhibit weak acidic character due to the 50 percent s-character pulling electron density toward the carbon nucleus.
concepts.key_idea: High electronegativity of sp-hybridized carbon stabilizes the conjugate carbanion base, enabling proton removal by strong bases.
question_patterns: why is ethyne acidic while ethene and ethane are not
arrange ethyne, ethene and ethane in decreasing order of acidity
how does sodium metal distinguish between terminal and non-terminal alkynes
explain the chemical reaction of ethyne with sodamide

solution_steps.action: compare hybridisation states of the carbon bearing the hydrogen
solution_steps.explain: sp carbon in alkynes has 50 percent s-character compared to 33 percent in sp2 and 25 percent in sp3.

solution_steps.action: evaluate carbanion stability and proton release
solution_steps.explain: greater electronegativity of sp carbon stabilizes the resulting acetylide anion, enabling reaction with Na or NaNH2 to liberate hydrogen gas or ammonia.

concepts.title: Directive Influence in Electrophilic Aromatic Substitution
concepts.definition: Substituents already present on a benzene ring determine the rate and orientation of subsequent electrophilic attack through inductive and resonance electron donation or withdrawal.
concepts.formula: Activating (+M, +I) -> ortho/para; Deactivating (-M, -I) -> meta (except halogens which are o/p)
concepts.key_idea: Resonance electron release enhances electron density specifically at both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both ortho and para positions, while electron-withdrawing groups deplete ortho/para positions more than meta.
question_patterns: explain the ortho and para directing influence of OH group in phenol
why is nitro group meta directing and deactivating
predict the major product when monosubstituted benzene undergoes nitration
arrange the given substituted benzenes in decreasing order of reactivity towards electrophiles

solution_steps.action: determine the electronic effect of the existing ring substituent
solution_steps.explain: classify substituent as electron donating (+R/+I like -OH, -NH2, -CH3) or electron withdrawing (-R/-I like -NO2, -COOH, -CHO).

solution_steps.action: predict attack position of the incoming electrophile
solution_steps.explain: activating and moderately deactivating halo groups direct to ortho/para; strong deactivating groups direct incoming electrophiles to meta.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Write IUPAC names of the products obtained by addition reactions of HBr to {alkene} in (i) the absence of peroxide and (ii) the presence of peroxide.

solution_template.action: apply Markovnikov addition in the absence of peroxide
solution_template.explain: the electrophile H+ adds to C-1 generating a secondary carbocation at C-2, yielding 2-bromohexane.

solution_template.action: apply anti-Markovnikov addition in the presence of peroxide
solution_template.explain: Br radical attacks C-1 generating a more stable secondary radical at C-2, yielding 1-bromohexane as the major product.
